newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: City of Prague seen to discuss intl bond on Friday.
newsitem.headline: City of Prague seen to discuss intl bond on Friday.

text.p: The Prague city council will discuss on Friday a decision on a proposed $300 million international bond issue, a spokeswoman for city hall told Reuters.
The spokewoman said the proposal was expected to get to the council by 12.00 p.m. (1000 GMT).

The city's executive sent a plan to the full city council on Thursday calling for a five to seven year international issue to finance transport infrastructure projects, but debate was recessed in the early evening before the issue came to the floor.
The government and central bank have criticised the idea.
No market or currency has been specified for the issue, which is expected to carry a coupon of around seven percent with an expected launch date in September or October.
An arranger for the issue should be chosen by a public tender.

Government and central bank officials have warned the city against going ahead with the issue because it would bring a large amount of new funds into circulation at a time when the economy is struggling to keep the money supply in check.

The Czech economy was shaken in late May by a speculative attack on the crown which forced the central bank to float the currency and it fell to more than 15 percent below its highs against the dollar and mark in early February.

The controlled float of the currency was backed by a rise in key interest rates and a government austerity package meant to slow domestic demand and dampen the inflationary effects of the crown's depreciation.
Prague carries an indicative investment-grade "A" rating from Standard & Poor's, the same as the Czech sovereign debt.
